title: Release train orchestrator: weekly slice, RC derivation, and roll-forward tooling
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Objective: Build an orchestrator and set of automation primitives to make the weekly release slice deterministic, produce Release Candidates (RCs) automatically, and enable safe roll-forwards and LTS channel tagging. Background: We currently run a manual weekly cut that requires on-call coordination, manual tagging, and hand-crafted release notes. This causes inconsistent windows, delayed rollouts, and occasional misses for patch backports. Scope: 1) A CI-driven 'weekly slice' job that collects merge window commits, computes semantic version bump candidates, and generates a draft RC tag. 2) Release Candidate derivation rules (how RCs differ across major/minor/LTS channels and how we annotate compatibility). 3) Automated release notes draft generation (Conventional Commits + changelog templates) with a human review step. 4) Roll-forward tooling that can automatically create a canary rollout and trigger backport patches for LTS channels when the RC is promoted. 5) Audit logging for private deployments and update metadata to support upgrades. Out of scope: full UI in Console for rollouts (will be follow-up), full on-prem automatic installer (partial hooks only). Deliverables: - CI pipeline changes (github actions/workflow) that run weekly-slice and publish candidate artifacts. - A release-orchestrator microservice (minimal) or GitHub Action to perform tagging and metadata publishing. - Release notes draft stored in /releases/drafts and a PR template for review. - Rollout policy scripts that call existing deployment hooks to start canaries and monitor metrics. Acceptance criteria: - Weekly slice job runs unattended and produces a draft RC tag and draft release notes at least 3 days before the scheduled publish date. - RC promotion requires explicit human approval via GitHub (merge button on release-draft PR). - LTS channel tagging applied according to the semantic policy (see 'notes') and backports created automatically for critical fixes. - All generated artifacts include metadata (commit range, build IDs, kernel/config hashes) for reproducibility.

changelog_strategy: Use Conventional Commits for automated categorization. release-drafter will generate draft notes that are reviewed via a generated PR. For structured output include 'consumer-impact' footers and a JSON metadata blob in the draft release assets.
rollout_gates: Gate 1: Smoke pass - health endpoints stable for 3 consecutive checks (1m intervals)
Gate 2: Telemetry SLOs - latency P95 and error-rate thresholds must be within 10% of baseline over 15m window
Gate 3: Canary traffic ramp - start at 1% traffic, canary must remain healthy for 60m before 5% ramp
Gate 4: Manual approval - RM/PM signoff is required for LTS promotions and critical customer-impact changes
notes: Versioning policy: semantic versioning with explicit LTS channels. LTS labels are applied to minor versions (eg. 1.12-lts) after N weeks of stable operation and SLO compliance.
RC derivation: An RC tag uses pattern vMAJOR.MINOR.PATCH-rc.N where N increments per candidate. RCs for LTS branches include branch metadata and a 'lts' label in release assets.
Backport strategy: Critical fixes auto-create cherry-pick PRs to LTS branches, but human review is required before merge. Backport PRs must include the original commit range and test results.
Trade-offs: Full automation reduces human error but increases risk of propagating flaky tests. We will build visibility and an easy 'abort' path before enabling auto-promotion for LTS channels.
Observability: Release metadata will include build ID, kernel/hash, quantization profile, and list of changed models to help triage regressions in telemetry.

Roll-forward vs rollback: Default strategy is roll-forward (patch-on-top) for hotfixes to preserve upgrade path; rollback is reserved for release windows where rolling forward would cause incompatibility.
Future work: integrate with Console rollout UI, provide SDK hooks for clients to opt into staged updates, and expand auditing for air-gapped Private installs.
